status: Implemented; broad default and Worker regressions passed
contract: An exclusive live reservation may shrink after released storage is dropped. No growth, reclamation, alias resizing or readmission is allowed. Live handle byte count is updated; consumed handle byte count remains historical.
implementation: Window key admission shrinks formatting scratch in place instead of partitioning into two new ownership handles.

validation.additionalStageTest: Added after the full suite; all three memory-shrink tests then passed. Shrinking does not recycle stage allocation allowance; externally held reservations outlive scope disposal.

benchmarks.finding: At 16384 unique numeric rows, local medians changed from mode 23.54ms / distinct 22.37ms to 15.29ms / 12.25ms. The rejected getter implementation was slower at 35.25ms / 33.73ms. Duplicate-heavy current cases remain around 6.4-6.7ms. Single local benchmark runs are directional evidence, not a cloud latency or total-heap claim. Further amortization remains open.

mutableLedgerFollowup.change: Partial mutable-ledger trimming now shrinks the existing exclusive handle instead of partitioning and releasing a new handle.
mutableLedgerFollowup.validation: 128 tests passed across mutable-memory-ledger, owned-aggregate-state and owned-group-directory; TypeScript build passed.
mutableLedgerFollowup.newTest: Partial trimming keeps the live handle, updates its bytes, preserves logical payload after repeated release/trim, and releases all usage on scope disposal. Partition is instrumented to throw if invoked.
mutableLedgerFollowup.reuseFinding: MutableMemoryLedger already provides chunked admission, exact-size fallback, bookkeeping charges, reclaimable spare capacity, mutation rollback and scope cleanup. Window integration should reuse this mechanism, preserving scope versus standalone-budget lifetime and admitting ledger metadata. Window per-value admission remains unchanged in this followup.
